LESSON: VEGETATION IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Vegetation in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Vegetation in Eastern Africa, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: How can we conserve vegetation in our environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the main types of vegetation in Eastern Africa on a map,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Vegetation in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: Learners follow instructions to locate the main vegetation types in Eastern Africa

using digital devices.

● Self-Efficacy: Learners identify general features in their locality as they plan and carry out activities on conservation of

vegetation within the locality.

10

Values:
● Responsibility: Learners show determination as they plant and care for vegetation school.

● Peace: Learners respect self and others as they discuss in groups to describe the characteristics of the main types of

vegetation in Eastern Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PICs):

● Environmental education: Learners practise environmental awareness as they plan and write down, in groups, how

they will conserve vegetation within the school compound.

● Patriotism: Learners demonstrate patriotism as they plan and carry out activities on conservation of vegetation in

their locality.

Links to other Learning Areas:
● Learners apply Integrated Science knowledge and skills to plant and care for vegetation at school.

● Learners use Creative Arts skills to draw and display in class a map indicating the main types of vegetation in Eastern

Africa.
